cd /home/mike/nexus-code; gh pr comment 51 --body "**Independent Review (\`claude-code\`, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)): CHANGES REQUESTED on \`b590be2\`**

Reviewer independence: I wrote no part of PLAN-12 or PR #48/#51. Read-only source review plus one local reproduction against \`tsc\` output of \`b590be2\`, in a scratch prefix. No SUITE claim, no inference, no held-out access.

### Blocking
**B1. Startup recovery bricks every launch of a non-writable install once any upgrade has completed.** \`performUpgrade\` leaves \`.upgrade-journal.json\` in place with \`state: \"complete\"\`. The new \`index.ts\` block calls \`recoverUpgrade(prefix)\` whenever that file exists. \`recoverUpgrade\` creates \`lib/nexus/.upgrade.lock\` (\`openSync(lock, \"wx\")\`) **before** \`recoverUpgradeLocked\` sees that the state needs no action. With an unwritable \`lib/nexus\` (e.g. \`NEXUS_PREFIX=/usr/local\` installed by root and run by a normal user, or a read-only mount), the open throws EACCES, the catch maps that to \`manual_intervention\`, and \`index.ts\` exits 2 on every non-\`--version\`/\`--help\` command. Reproduction (valid journal, state complete):
\`\`\`
writable lib  -> {\"recovered\":false,\"action\":\"none\",\"details\":\"No interrupted upgrade found in journal.\"}
read-only lib -> {\"recovered\":false,\"action\":\"manual_intervention\",\"details\":\"EACCES: permission denied, open '…/lib/nexus/.upgrade.lock'\"}
\`\`\`
Suggested fix: on startup, read and validate the journal first and return immediately for \`idle\`/\`complete\`/\`rolled_back\`, before any lock or write. Take the lock only when recovery will actually act. Add a regression test: a completed journal in a 0555 \`lib/nexus\` must start normally. Separately, as written, every ordinary launch creates and unlinks a file in the install tree, which conflicts with the \"read-only commands never write state\" intent.

### Non-blocking
- **N1. Misleading refusal during a concurrent upgrade.** If one terminal is inside \`nexus upgrade\` (live lock PID), a \`nexus\` launch in another terminal exits 2 with \"Run nexus upgrade --recover after resolving the recorded failure\". Nothing has failed. Suggest a distinct message such as \"upgrade in progress\".
- **N2. Stale-lock takeover is not atomic.** In \`recoverUpgrade\`, two processes that both see a dead holder PID can each \`unlinkSync\` and then \`openSync(\"wx\")\` in turn; B's unlink can remove A's fresh lock, so both run \`recoverUpgradeLocked\` concurrently (e.g. several panes starting after a crash). A loser that sees \`displacedTargetDir\` present then writes \`recovery_required\` over the winner's \`rolled_back\`. Suggest taking over via an atomic rename of a uniquely named lock, or re-reading the lock after \`wx\` succeeds and verifying the PID.

content.text:
I've asked for changes on PR #51, the rework of upgrade rollback and crash recovery. Once any upgrade has completed, every `nexus` command exits with code 2 if the user can't write to the install directory, as in a root-owned `/usr/local` install. The default per-user install isn't affected.

- **The blocking bug.** After a successful upgrade, the upgrade journal stays on disk. The new startup check runs on every launch and creates a lock file in the install directory before it checks whether anything needs recovering. I compiled the PR and ran a small reproduction: with a writable directory it returns "nothing to recover", and with a read-only one it fails with a permission error. The installer accepts any install location through `NEXUS_PREFIX`, so this setup can happen. The fix is to check the journal first and take the lock only when recovery will actually act. I also suggested a regression test.
- **Non-blocking notes.**
  - Starting `nexus` while another terminal is upgrading gives a misleading "resolve the recorded failure" message.
  - Two processes clearing a stale lock at the same moment can both end up running recovery.
  - Kept rollback copies of the package are never cleaned up.
  - There's a small gap in killing a hung version check.

Everything else I checked in the PR looks right. The review is posted on #51 and recorded in the coordination log. I removed the scratch worktree.

Other work since the last update:
- The plan-doc fix for 9 fault classes is up as #50, with an independent approval.
- The older upgrade PR #48 has a request for changes from opencode.
- codex-api-root is fixing a flaky Rust symlink-race test that failed on CI for integration commit 2fb069d.

**What I checked and accept:** the two-reclaimer handoff. With the mkdir gate, the inode re-check, and the holder-PID re-check, only one of two processes that both observe the same dead holder can unlink and re-acquire. The PID check also covers inode reuse after unlink. The ownership-checked release (inode + token) means a process can no longer delete a foreign lock. \`EPERM\` on the probe now counts as live. \`lockHeld\` re-entry from \`performUpgrade\`'s catch still skips acquisition and release. CI passes on 20/22/24, CodeQL and contest.

**N2b (should fix before accept): a crashed reclaimer wedges every later upgrade and recovery permanently.** \`.upgrade.lock.reclaim\` is removed only in the reclaimer's own \`finally\`; nothing else deletes it (\`git grep reclaim\` finds only the creators). If the reclaimer dies by SIGKILL or power loss after \`mkdir(reclaimDir)\` while a lock file still exists, every later caller sees \`EEXIST\`, waits 200 ms, and gives up. That window runs from the stale read to the unlink, or from \`acquire()\` to the \`rmdir\`. I re-reviewed PR #51 (upgrade recovery) at 5e6d1f4, as opencode asked, and requested one more small fix.

- **The concurrency fix works.** When two processes find the same stale lock left by a dead process, only one of them now takes it over. A process can also no longer delete a lock that another process owns. CI passes on Node 20, 22 and 24.
- **What still needs fixing.** The takeover creates a temporary marker directory, `.upgrade.lock.reclaim`. If the process doing the takeover is killed or loses power before removing it, nothing ever deletes it. From then on, `nexus upgrade --recover` reports "upgrade in progress" forever and `nexus upgrade` refuses to run. Neither message names the directory, so a user can't find the cause. I reproduced this on a build of the PR. That's the kind of crash this PR is meant to make recoverable.
- **Suggested fix.** Record the owner inside that marker so a later process can clear it once the owner is dead or the marker is old, and add a regression test. At minimum, name the directory in the error message.

The review is posted on #51 and recorded in the log. I also widened the log watch so it catches review requests written in any form, including `REVIEW_REQUEST`.

content.text:
v1.0.0 is not releasable yet. The source code is close to ready, but almost none of the required testing on a release candidate (RC) has started, because no RC has been built. I checked integration as it stands now, at `2007b90`, where the package version is still `0.1.0-alpha.2`. Only `v0.1.0-alpha.1` and `v0.1.0-alpha.2` are tagged.

The requirements check (`check_requirements.mjs --enforce`) fails at that commit: 11 of 123 requirements are below the bar.

## 1. Source work still open
- **PR #56: version-check permissions for the evaluator account.** It needs CI and an independent review. I'm not independent for this one.
- **PR #50: plan-doc fix for the 9 fault classes.** It's approved; it only needs a base refresh and green CI.
- **The PR #54 hold:** the version check run as a separate user couldn't find its workspace. That's what #56 fixes.
- PR #51 (upgrade recovery) and PR #55 merged in the last half hour, and PR #33 (evaluator boundary) merged earlier.

## 2. Building the RC (codex-api-root, as release publisher)
- Bump the version to `1.0.0-rc.1` and tag it. The release workflow then builds the RC as a prerelease.
- Run the RC artifact checks: supply chain, SBOM, reproducible packaging, and the release security scan (REQ-REL-005).
- Run the two-runner reproducibility build on the exact RC tag (REQ-REL-114, issue #5).

## 3. Testing the installed RC, with no RC yet (issue #2)

| Requirement | What's needed |
|---|---|
| REQ-QUAL-101 | Held-out T2: 40 tasks × 5 runs. The evaluator and host are now ready. |
| REQ-QUAL-109 | T3 long tasks: 8 × 5. False absence and false presence must both be 0, and steering must be at least 95%. |
| REQ-AGT-002 | Zero false VERIFIED, measured on the T2, T3 and T4 runs, including the 9 × 5 fault matrix. |
| REQ-QUAL-107, REQ-PRV-003 | Standalone runs through the proxy (plain, llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama profiles), plus a live run without homelab-ai. |
| REQ-PRV-111 | `providers verify` plus one live task on the pinned OpenRouter model; ChatGPT verify repeated on the RC. |

The T2 runs alone are about 840 runs, roughly 4 days of continuous inference on the single gateway. This is the longest stretch on the critical path.

## 4. Things only people can do
- **REQ-QUAL-108 (issue #3): you, at real terminals.** 5 environments × 3 sizes on the installed RC, with screenshots. Automated tests can't stand in for this.
- **REQ-AGT-110 (issue #6): continuity and truncation acceptance** by a reviewer who didn't build that work. That rules out me and the other agents who implemented it. Someone needs to be named.
- **REQ-AGT-010:** the ledger owner has to record a status decision under DEC-04 against the current commit.
- **The custodian** has to add per-repo license records to the held-out custody reports (issue #1).
- **You (admin):** apply the branch and tag rulesets from PR #23.

## 5. Final gate (issue #7)
Once everything above passes: update the requirements ledger until `--enforce` passes, finish the docs checklist, and make a stable `v1.0.0` commit that changes only the version. That release is created as a draft, and the publisher then publishes it and checks the published assets and installer.

**Bottom line:** after #56 and #50, the next real step is building the RC. Then come the qualification runs, which take days of inference. Your terminal matrix and the independent continuity review can run alongside those.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# The sandbox requires --disable-userns. Ubuntu 22.04's bubblewrap 0.6.1 predates
# that option. Build a patched upstream release when the packaged executable
# lacks it; releases before 0.12.0 are affected by CVE-2026-87766.
readonly BWRAP=/usr/bin/bwrap
readonly SOURCE_URL=https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/releases/download/v0.13.1/bubblewrap-0.13.1.tar.xz
readonly SOURCE_SHA256=0e85c8702248b8dd64144f594147553650cdd0e4c951690345faace79c217c4d

supports_required_userns_control() {
  [[ -x "$BWRAP" ]] || return 1

  local version_output major minor patch
  version_output=$("$BWRAP" --version 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$version_output" =~ bubblewrap[[:space:]]+([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+) ]] || return 1
  major=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
  minor=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
  patch=${BASH_REMATCH[3]}
  ((major > 0 || minor > 12 || (minor == 12 && patch >= 0))) || return 1
  "$BWRAP" --help 2>&1 | grep -Fq -- '--disable-userns'
}

if supports_required_userns_control; then
  "$BWRAP" --version
  exit 0
fi

work="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/nexus-bubblewrap.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
archive="$work/bubblewrap-0.13.1.tar.xz"

curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --retry 3 "$SOURCE_URL" -o "$archive"
printf '%s  %s\n' "$SOURCE_SHA256" "$archive" | sha256sum --check --status
tar -xJf "$archive" -C "$work"
meson setup "$work/build" "$work/bubblewrap-0.13.1" \
  --prefix=/usr \
  -Dtests=false \
  -Dselinux=disabled \
  -Dbash_completion=disabled \
  -Dzsh_completion=disabled \
  -Dman=disabled
ninja -C "$work/build"

# The build runs as the unprivileged CI user. Only the resulting executable is
# installed into the ephemeral runner, without setuid permissions.
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0755 "$work/build/bwrap" "$BWRAP"
"$BWRAP" --version | grep -F '0.13.1'

PR #56's code isn't the cause of its CI failure. The failing test passes on mike-dev as `nobody` with the same 0711 temporary storage mount and runtime directory CI uses. That leaves the sandbox tool, bubblewrap, as the remaining difference: CI builds version 0.13.1 from source, while mike-dev has the packaged 0.9.0. I couldn't prove it, because building 0.13.1 here would mean installing development packages on the qualification host, and I didn't do that.

- **Next step for the owner:** I posted on #56 a short diagnostic CI step that tests bubblewrap's mount of the workspace directly as `nobody`, so the next CI run can confirm or rule this out.
- **Security concern on #56:** its new fallback removes the access-control entries and makes evaluator workspaces readable by every local user. I asked the reviewer to confirm that's acceptable or have it fail closed instead.
- **Host finding (posted on #49):** mike-dev runs bubblewrap 0.9.0. The repo's own CI script says versions before 0.12.0 are affected by CVE-2026-87766, and the host setup scripts never check this. So qualification would run its sandbox on a version the project considers vulnerable, and on a different version from CI. Upgrading the host binary is a decision for the host owner, so I haven't touched it.

The temporary mount and directories are removed, and I've released the SUITE lock.

Elsewhere, PR #59 (session IDs now from a secure random generator) is approved with green CI. PR #60 (ties the requirements gate to RC evidence, +315 lines) is new and unreviewed. I'll review #60 once its CI runs. The log watch now covers both the plain and JSON entry formats.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Return the number of processes in a terminal test's systemd scope. A zero is
+# emitted only when the scope is proven empty or systemd confirms it is gone.
+nexus_terminal_scope_procs() {
+  local unit="$1"
+  local cgroup_root="${NEXUS_CGROUP_ROOT:-/sys/fs/cgroup}"
+  local load_state active_state control_group process_file count
+
+  load_state="$(systemctl --user show --property=LoadState --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+  if [[ "$load_state" == "not-found" ]]; then
+    printf '0\n'
+    return 0
+  fi
+  [[ "$load_state" == "loaded" ]] || return 2
+
+  active_state="$(systemctl --user show --property=ActiveState --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+  control_group="$(systemctl --user show --property=ControlGroup --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+
+  if [[ -n "$control_group" ]]; then
+    [[ "$control_group" == /* && "$control_group" != *"/../"* && "$control_group" != */.. ]] || return 2
+    process_file="${cgroup_root%/}${control_group}/cgroup.procs"
+    if [[ -f "$process_file" && -r "$process_file" ]]; then
+      count="$(awk 'BEGIN { invalid = 0 } { if ($0 !~ /^[0-9]+$/) invalid = 1 } END { if (invalid) exit 2; print NR }' "$process_file")" || return 2
+      printf '%s\n' "$count"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  # A stopped, loaded unit with no remaining cgroup has no processes. An
+  # active unit with missing/unreadable cgroup data is an unknown measurement.
+  if [[ "$active_state" == "inactive" && -z "$control_group" ]]; then
+    printf '0\n'
+    return 0
+  fi
+  return 2
+}
